sections.h2: Which office bills property tax for West Palm Beach homes?
sections.html:
West Palm Beach sits in Palm Beach County, so the Palm Beach County Tax Collector sends the bill and the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser sets the value. The city only sets its own millage rate. According to the tax collector, the season opens with the TRIM notice in August and the office mails more than 600,000 bills by November 1.

Bills go to the address the property appraiser holds. If you moved or sold, fix the address, or file the collector's Property Sold Form so the bill is forwarded to the new owner.

The revenue is distributed to the county and city governments, the school district, fire departments, libraries, parks, children's services and the healthcare district, per the collector's property tax page.

sections.h2: What millage rates apply to West Palm Beach?
sections.html:
The property appraiser publishes a table of every taxing authority's rates. For West Palm Beach it lists a final 2025 city rate of 8.1308 mills and a proposed 2026 rate of 8.1308. A mill is $1 of tax per $1,000 of taxable value. Treat the 2026 column as proposed, and ask the tax collector when the final figure is certified.

Your bill is the total of everything that touches your parcel, so use the parcel lookup instead of adding columns.

sections.h2: When are West Palm Beach property taxes due?
sections.html:
Payable from November 1 through March 31, with a sliding discount. The tax collector's schedule runs 4% in November, 3% in December, 2% in January and 1% in February, with no discount in March, and delinquency starting in April.

When a date falls on a weekend or holiday, state law moves the deadline to the next business day. Once a bill is delinquent it cannot be paid online. Payments must be received by the last working day of the month to count for that month, and the postmark is no longer proof of payment.

The gross amount is due March 31 with no discount. The office also publishes an important dates page, so check it before you plan a closing near a deadline.

sections.h2: What happens to delinquent taxes in Palm Beach County?
sections.html:
After April 1 the tax carries penalties and interest, and later the collector sells a tax certificate. By Florida statute 197.402, the sale is held 60 days after the delinquency date or June 1, whichever is later, per the collector.

  • The certificate is a first lien that an investor buys by paying the tax.
  • Certificates nobody buys are struck to the county, and those accrue 18% a year, or 1.5% a month.
  • To redeem, pay the delinquent tax, the accrued interest, advertising costs and a $6.25 collection fee.
  • If the tax stays unpaid for two years from delinquency, the holder may apply for a tax deed under s. 197.502.

The Clerk and Comptroller conducts the tax deed sale, and an owner can redeem before the sale occurs. Two further statewide points: the clerk's auction requires a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater, with full payment within 24 hours per s. 197.542.

sections.h2: How do homestead rules affect a West Palm Beach sale?
sections.html:
A homestead exemption belongs to the owner who lives there as of January 1 and ends when the house sells. Florida's homestead guide says the exemption is up to $50,000, with the first $25,000 applying to school taxes too, and that applications go to the property appraiser by March 1.

The Save Our Homes cap limits yearly growth in assessed value to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change, and a sale resets the assessment to just value the next January 1. A seller moving within Florida may carry some of that benefit to a new home. Portability needs the new homestead established within three years, with Form DR-501T filed alongside DR-501, per the Save Our Homes guide.

The county collector's home page also directs owners to a statewide amendment on property tax. Ask the collector which changes affect your parcel before you plan around them.

sections.h2: What costs come with a deed in West Palm Beach?
sections.html:
The deed is taxed at 70 cents per $100 of consideration, because Palm Beach County is not Miami-Dade, according to the Department of Revenue. Consideration includes any mortgage on the property, whether or not the buyer assumes it. The Department says all parties are liable regardless of who agrees to pay.

The clerk also charges recording fees. The statute sets $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, plus a trust fund charge and a per-page technology charge, per s. 28.24.

The title agent will total both on the settlement statement. Ask who pays deed stamps under your contract before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: What should a West Palm Beach seller do about back taxes?
sections.html:
Ask the tax collector for a written payoff through the closing date, and check whether a certificate exists. The collector's delinquent list is posted online, and county-held certificates can be searched through its RealAuction link.

  • Pay before April 1 if you can, to avoid penalties.
  • Redeem a certificate before a tax deed application is filed.
  • Have the title agent pay the payoff from your proceeds at closing.

Delinquent amounts cannot be paid online, so allow time for an in-person or mailed payment before the last working day of the month.

faqs.q: What is the West Palm Beach city millage rate?
faqs.a: The Palm Beach County Property Appraiser's table lists 8.1308 mills as the final 2025 rate and 8.1308 as the proposed 2026 rate. Your total bill adds the county, school and other levies.

faqs.q: When does West Palm Beach property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. The Palm Beach County Tax Collector says delinquent tax is subject to penalties and interest and cannot be paid online.

faqs.q: What discount can I get on a West Palm Beach tax bill?
faqs.a: 4% in November, 3% in December, 2% in January and 1% in February. March carries no discount.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to redeem a tax certificate in Palm Beach County?
faqs.a: You pay the delinquent tax, accrued interest, advertising costs and a $6.25 collection fee, according to the tax collector.

faqs.q: Who runs the tax deed sale in Palm Beach County?
faqs.a: The Clerk and Comptroller. A certificate holder may apply for a tax deed after two years from the delinquency date, and the owner may redeem until the sale.
